_why: permission: 'read' MCP tools known to change persisted state (see test/integration/mcp-read-tools-do-not-mutate.test.js). This list only shrinks: fix a tool, then remove it here. kind 'write' changes rows of the tables in its 'tables' list, and the test fails if it changes anything else or stops writing a listed table; kind 'init' only creates empty structure (a table or index, a database with no rows, a directory) on first use, and the test fails if an 'init' tool ever changes more than that. No 'write' entry is left, and test/mcp/tool-annotations.test.js fails if one is added: tools/list advertises every read tool read-only, so a read tool that changes rows must be declared 'write' instead.

violations.reason: Creates <cwd>/.stateset/treasury/treasury.db (schema, no rows) on first use -- under the process working directory, not beside the server's --db.
First audit tool to run opens the scoped audit store, creating <db>.audit.db (schema, no rows).
First circuit-breaker tool to run creates the empty a2a_circuit_breaker_events and a2a_spending_ledger tables and their indexes.
First agent-catalog tool to run creates the empty agent_catalog table and its indexes.
Creates the empty <db dir>/.stateset/a2a-checkpoints directory on first use.

_unreached: Read tools no sweep input gets to a successful handler run, so the sweep cannot say whether they write. Each needs something the sandbox does not have. With this checkout's own engine binding, the test fails when any other read tool never runs to success (a coverage regression) and when a listed tool does (remove it here). An engine binary built from another tree changes which tools reach, so the per-tool check is skipped there.
